relevance_map.reason: Untitled intro with generic product context; no driver details.
Title page marketing line; adds no extractable driver data.
Part name only; no operational or register content.
Basic device description may confirm sensor type and output style.
Feature list can hint at interface, modes, and supported operating behavior.
Application examples are not needed for polling driver logic.
Absolute max ratings constrain safe operating limits and power handling.
Operating conditions define valid supply and ambient ranges for use.
Electrical specs can contain measurement current, resolution, and supply limits.
Reference data may support lux response behavior and scaling interpretation.
Block diagram can confirm internal flow but usually yields little code detail.
Diagram notes mention data register and interface behavior useful for command flow.
Measurement procedure likely describes command order and startup steps.
Instruction set table defines opcodes and command meanings directly used by driver.
Measurement modes table gives mode selection, timing, and resolution mapping.
Mode recommendation helps choose default settings and accuracy tradeoffs.
Reset command and async reset behavior affect startup and recovery sequencing.
Explains reset command usage and when it is valid after power-up.
Power supply sequencing impacts reset and bus bring-up timing.
Recommended supply timing may be needed for init and power-on handling.
Contains I2C transaction details, ACK behavior, and don't-care states for bus reads.
Application circuit example may clarify wiring for reset and supply pins.
Short example header with no technical content to extract.
Reset IC example informs hardware reset integration but not core driver logic.
Fragmentary heading only; no usable content.
Different supply example may matter for board-level reset and power sequencing.
I2C bus access section is core for transaction format and command access.
Interface timing chart can supply bus setup/hold requirements if present.
Slave address section is required to configure I2C address bits.
Write format shows exact I2C write frame and command byte placement.
Read format tables define read transaction, return bytes, and command side effects.
Input measurement command table likely contains opcodes, modes, and MTreg scaling.
Terminal description can confirm pin roles for wiring and power/reset handling.
Package outline is mechanical only and not needed for driver generation.
General caution section is mostly handling guidance, not driver behavior.
Duplicate caution on absolute max ratings; no added driver logic value.
GND voltage caution can affect valid logic levels and board grounding.
Manufacturing caution about shorts/mounting is not driver-facing.
EMI caution is application guidance, not relevant to polling driver code.
Inspection/process notes are manufacturing oriented and not driver data.
Input terminal limits may inform permissible voltages and pin behavior.
Thermal design advice is board-level guidance, not driver logic.
Package treatment instructions are handling notes, not code-relevant.
Rush current can matter for power sequencing and regulator sizing.
Exposed pad handling may affect grounding and assembly, not protocol.
Ordering section is commercial metadata, not driver content.
Part number listing is irrelevant to runtime driver generation.
Legal notes and disclaimers do not help implement the driver.
Support/contact page is not needed for extraction.

extraction_plan: Prioritize I2C protocol, slave address, write/read frames, command set, reset, and MTreg/mode tables; then pull timing, electrical limits, and pin roles for safe polling-driver init/read handling.
extraction_notes: No explicit register map; treat commands/opcodes as registers_or_commands. Confirm whether DVI is a typo for VCC in outline. Use conservative defaults for MTreg and measurement mode if ambiguous.
